title: spec review: S2i v2 harness_depth and small-task fast path in shadow: deterministic depth level 0-4 from persisted task fields, fast path skips the Jev shadow-context call and Claude-fallback skill routing for level 0-1, promotion feature fast_path (P24, P25, P26)
spec:
Respec of T-1018 (spec review T-1070 request_changes folded; T-1018 was never executed). Create orchestrator/harness_depth.py. level(task, *, cfg, history) -> {"level": 0..4, "reasons": [...], "eligible_fast_path": bool, "would_skip": [...]}. Deterministic rules, first match wins, every input a field that is actually persisted on bus tasks (never constraints.architectural, which no task carries): 4 when the task is a goal container (constraints.goal true), any scope path matches a [review] security_paths glob or a [review] migrations glob if present, or complexity >= 8; 3 when complexity is 6-7, any depends_on task lacks merged_into, or constraints.route == "spec_review"; 2 when complexity is 4-5; 1 when complexity <= 3, scope has at most 3 paths, no security path and no unresolved dependency; 0 additionally when every acceptance line except the tests-green gate line is a test id of the form tests/test_x.py::test_y and history for constraints.task_class has first_pass_rate >= 0.8 with first_pass_defined_count >= 5 (the count of rows where first_pass is known, not n). Missing or thin history means level 1, never 0. history is a plain dict {task_class: {"first_pass_rate", "first_pass_defined_count"}} that the caller computes once per daemon tick from scorecard rows (add one helper harness_depth.history_by_task_class(rows) and call it once in the dispatch tick, passing the result to every candidate; never rescan history per task). would_skip names only real call sites: "jev_shadow_context" (daemon._dispatch_worker's jev_route.shadow_context and record_shadow calls) and "skill_routing" (spawn.run_worker's _prepare_skills call for the execute role, the Claude-fallback executor path). Nothing else is claimed or skipped; strategy lookup and scout suggestions do not exist on the dispatch path and are not mentioned. Fast path = level 0 or 1. [harness].depth_mode = "shadow" in .orchestrator/pool.toml with a dated comment (off|shadow|active). shadow: per execute dispatch write one decision_log row kind "harness_depth" (add to KINDS) with candidates 0..4, selected level, reasons, would_skip; change nothing a worker sees. active: for eligible tasks skip exactly the two named call sites and stamp pipeline.harness_level; hooks, tests-green, security review by path, spec review and the human PR are untouched in every mode. promotion FEATURES entry "fast_path": activation criteria at least 20 shadow harness_depth rows at level 0-1 and, once active, first-pass rate of fast-path tasks not below the shadow baseline and lower median tokens per accepted task; demotion when any fast-path task takes two fix rounds; self-refusing (active with unmet criteria runs as shadow and notifies). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/15-harness-depth.md with the rules table, the two skip sites by function name, and the level distribution over this repository's merged execute tasks (compute with level() over every merged execute task in .orchestrator/tasks and tabulate counts per level).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Read the merged modules (decision_log.py KINDS, promotion.py FEATURES and mode(), daemon._dispatch_worker, spawn.run_worker, scorecard._routing_group) before building on them; interface contracts are in .orchestrator/plan.md section GOAL T-0991.
acceptance: tests/test_harness_depth.py::test_levels_from_rules (goal container 4, security path task 4, complexity 6 task 3, spec_review route task 3, complexity 5 task 2, small localized task 1, small task with test-id acceptance and history first_pass_rate 0.9 over 6 defined rows 0)
tests/test_harness_depth.py::test_missing_or_thin_history_never_yields_level_zero (no history, and history with first_pass_defined_count 4, both give level 1)
tests/test_harness_depth.py::test_history_by_task_class_uses_defined_count (rows with first_pass None are excluded from first_pass_defined_count)

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_records_harness_depth_row_in_shadow_and_changes_nothing (one decision_log row kind harness_depth per dispatch; jev_route.shadow_context still called; packet identical)

tests/test_daemon.py::test_active_fast_path_skips_jev_shadow_context_but_keeps_security_review (active mode, level 1 task: jev_route.shadow_context not called, pipeline.harness_level stamped, reviews_expected unchanged for a security-path diff)
tests/test_spawn.py::test_active_fast_path_skips_skill_routing_for_execute_role (active mode, level 1 task: _prepare_skills not called on the execute role; review role still calls it)
tests/test_promotion.py::test_fast_path_feature_registered (FEATURES has fast_path with the criteria above; mode() returns shadow from pool.toml)

risks.issue: Level-3 rule 'constraints.route == "spec_review"' references a field that is not persisted anywhere in this repo — grepped orchestrator/*.py, .orchestrator/tasks/*.json, and .claude/skills for constraints.route/"route" and found zero writers of it. The spec itself explicitly warns against exactly this mistake ('never constraints.architectural, which no task carries'), but constraints.route is the same kind of invented field. No task-creation path (write-spec, bus_create_task, goals.py) sets it.

The level-3 rule 'any depends_on task lacks merged_into' is unreachable at the only call site the spec defines. harness_depth.level() only runs 'per execute dispatch' (shadow mode) inside _dispatch_worker (daemon.py:532), which is only reached for tasks that already passed eligible()->bus.ready() (daemon.py:674-685, bus.py:140-150), and bus.ready() already requires every depends_on task to be merged_into (or done) before the task becomes a dispatch candidate. So by the time level() sees the task, this condition can never be true. test_levels_from_rules also has no sub-case for it, so it would ship untested and effectively dead.

Spec says level 4 fires on 'any scope path matches ... a [review] migrations glob if present', but pool.toml has no top-level [review].migrations key — the migrations glob lives at [review.areas.migrations].paths (line 108-110), nested under 'areas' alongside auth/interfaces/data_deletion. 'if present' plus the wrong key path leaves the insertion point ambiguous: an implementer could reasonably look for cfg['review']['migrations'] and always find nothing.

Spec describes fast_path as 'self-refusing (active with unmet criteria runs as shadow and notifies)', implying a runtime auto-downgrade when [harness].depth_mode=active but promotion criteria aren't met. But every existing FEATURES/mode() consumer (skill_routing, jev_routing, etc.) only reads the configured mode verbatim (current_mode/mode(), lines 69-85) — evaluate() is advisory-only and never overrides config. The concrete 'active:' rule in the spec ('for eligible tasks skip exactly the two named call sites and stamp pipeline.harness_level') never mentions consulting promotion.evaluate('fast_path', ...) before trusting depth_mode. No acceptance test exercises self-refusal either (test_fast_path_feature_registered only checks the FEATURES entry exists and mode() reads shadow). This is either an unimplemented promise or a name collision with the existing advisory-only pattern.

Skipping _prepare_skills entirely for fast-path execute tasks (line 1236) also means no 'skill_selection' decision_log row is ever recorded for those tasks. promotion.collect('skill_routing') (promotion.py:183-188) counts exactly those rows to build skill_routing's own promotion evidence. Once harness_depth goes active, skill_routing's sample silently shrinks and skews toward only non-fast-path (complex) tasks, with no acknowledgment of this cross-feature interaction in the spec.

suggested_spec_changes: Drop the constraints.route == 'spec_review' sub-rule, or name the real persisted field it should read (none currently exists); if this needs to be new, scope a task to add it as a genuine bus-task field before harness_depth depends on it.

Either remove the 'any depends_on task lacks merged_into' branch (it is dead code at the defined per-dispatch call site) or specify a second, earlier call site where it is actually reachable, and add a dedicated acceptance test for it.
Fix the migrations glob reference to cfg['review']['areas']['migrations']['paths'] (pool.toml has no top-level [review].migrations key).

Either drop the 'self-refusing' runtime-downgrade language for fast_path, or add a concrete rule naming which call site checks promotion.evaluate('fast_path', ...) before honoring active mode, plus an acceptance test for the downgrade-and-notify path.

Acknowledge the skill_routing evidence-starvation interaction: note in the spec that active fast-path will shrink/bias collect('skill_routing')'s sample, or explicitly exempt fast-path tasks from that feature's promotion accounting.
